How to use

  • Diffuse 4 drops in the hour before sleep.
  • Dilute to 2% and massage into the soles of the feet.
  • Add 3 drops to a wool dryer ball for scented linens.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Scent profile

  • Dry cedar
  • Sweet balsam
  • Faint smoke

What's in it

  • 100% pure Cedrus atlantica wood oil

Who it's for

People who dislike sweet scents

Dry and woody with very little sweetness, which makes it a rare option if florals and citrus are not for you.

Anyone building a base note

Sits underneath brighter oils and holds them in place, so a citrus blend lasts longer than citrus alone.

Larger rooms

Diffuses slowly and evenly, where sharper oils can fill a small room and then vanish.

What people get wrong

Expecting a pencil-shaving smell. That is Virginian cedarwood, a different tree entirely. Atlas cedar is softer, sweeter and more resinous, and the two are not substitutes for one another despite sharing a name.

Using it as a top note. It is slow and heavy, so adding it last to a blend tends to flatten everything above it. Build it in first and layer the brighter oils over the top.

What it won't do

There are at least four unrelated trees sold as cedarwood — Atlas, Virginian, Texan and Chinese. If you have used cedarwood before and expect this to smell the same, check which one it was.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Cedarwood Grounding

Is this the same cedarwood used in wardrobes?

Usually not. The timber in moth-repellent blocks is typically Virginian cedar, which is actually a juniper. Ours is Cedrus atlantica, a true cedar from the Atlas mountains, with a softer and sweeter smell.

Why does it smell different from the last cedarwood I bought?

Almost certainly a different species. Atlas, Virginian, Texan and Chinese cedarwood are all sold under the same common name and smell noticeably different. The botanical name on the label is the only reliable guide.

Does it work in a blend with citrus?

Well, and it is one of the more useful things you can do with it. Cedarwood slows down how quickly citrus disappears, so an orange or grapefruit blend holds together for considerably longer.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Around 2% for the body — roughly 12 drops per 30 ml of carrier oil — and 1% for the face. Always patch-test before wider use, and never apply neat.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.
